newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Tuntex plans Asia's premier design centre.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Tuntex plans Asia's premier design centre.

text.p: Tuntex Distinct Corp, a major Taiwan industrial group, said on Monday it was launching Asia's biggest "design centre" in February with an eye to the huge construction markets in southeast Asia and China.

"The market is unlimited, especially with Taiwan executives everywhere in this region playing important roles," John Kao, chairman of Tuntex affiliate Eastern Start International Development Corp, said in an interview.

Taiwan investors have poured billions of dollars into projects in Southeast Asia and China and construction is the basis for all of them, Kao told Reuters in Tuntex's sparkling new Asia Pacific Design Centre in northern Taipei.

Construction of the 33,000-square-metre (325,000 sq-ft) centre was completed in December and the glass and steel complex can house more than 300 retailers, wholesalers, importers and exporters in construction-related industries.

The T$11 billion complex has exhibition halls, show stands, business centres, restaurants and a supermarket, making it one of the biggest investments by Tuntex, which already ranks as Taiwan's biggest land developer.

"The idea is to offer developers one-stop shopping for all they need," said Kao. "We can offer efficiency in addition to professional services and help Taiwan to become a real regional operations centre."
Taiwan launched an ambitious Asia Pacific Operation Centre project in 1995, aiming to lure the regional hubs of big multinational firms in a challenge to Hong Kong and Singapore.
Taiwan has promised to increase government efficiency to lure international companies to set up regional headquarters on the island.
